title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Scheduling, Profiling & Benchmarking Playbook
author: Elena Martínez
content:
Overview

This consolidated playbook documents Redwood Inference's serving runtime: high-level architecture, kernel selection and scheduling heuristics, profiling and regression playbooks, the benchmarking suite, release notes overview, known issues, and operational runbooks. The intent is to provide on-call engineers, performance owners, and SREs with a single reference for diagnosing performance regressions, tuning throughput/latency tradeoffs, and running standardized benchmarks for capacity planning.

1) Runtime architecture — key components

- Short intro: the serving runtime is a GPU-optimized inference engine (service name: rdinferd) that exposes the Redwood inference API and runs on Dedicated and Hosted pools.
- Components:
  - rdinferd (inference daemon): request handling, KV-cache management, batching, model kernel selection.
  - scheduler (rd-sched): per-node multi-tenant scheduler that enforces SLO-aware batching and GPU kernel placement.
  - cache-service (rd-kvcache): shared prefix + KV cache, pinned per-tenant shards.
  - router (rd-router): global request router for model variant fallbacks and region-aware routing.

- SLOs and targets (global):
  - 50th p50 latency target: 50ms for small models (<=2B) under steady state.
  - 95th p95 latency target: 150ms for small models (<=2B).
  - 99th p99 latency target: 200ms for medium models (2B-13B).
  - Throughput SLOs vary by Dedicated tier; see capacity table below.

2) Kernel selection & scheduling heuristics

- Goals: minimize p99 latency while maximizing GPU utilization and controlling cost.
- Kernel selection factors: model architecture, sequence length distribution, quantization profile, device compute capability, available workspace memory.
- Heuristics (summary):
  1. If avg_seq_len < 128 and batch_size <= 8 => use fast-fused attention kernel (kernel=fused_attn_v2).
  2. If model quantized (int8) and device supports tensorcore int8 path => kernel=tensorcore_int8; otherwise fall back to fused_attn_v1.
  3. For long-context workloads (avg_seq_len > 1024) prefer chunked-attention kernels with KV-sharding enabled.

- Scheduler policies (rd-sched configs):
  - latency-first: prioritize dispatching small batches to minimize tail latency.
  - throughput-first: aggressive batching up to batch_limit to maximize tokens/sec.
  - balanced: dynamic mode that trades off latency and utilization based on rolling 5-min SLA error budget.

Example scheduler config (YAML):
```yaml
policy: balanced
batch_limit: 32
max_latency_ms: 250
min_batch_fill_ms: 8
kv_cache_eviction_ms: 600000
kernel_selection: auto
```

3) Profiling playbook (how to triage performance regressions)

- Quick checklist (for on-call):
  1. Verify incident scope: which model, which pool, which region, any rollout events?
  2. Check rdinferd logs for kernel selection decisions and scheduling latencies (log path: /var/log/rdinferd/runtime.log).
  3. Run lightweight profiler: rd-profiler collect --trace=short --duration=30s --model <model-id> --node <node-id>.
  4. If KV cache miss rate > 5% for a cache-sensitive workload, consider warming with rd-kvcache prefetch.

- rd-profiler example usage:
```bash
# short trace: aggregated per-component timing
rd-profiler collect --trace=short --model redwood-mistral-3b --duration 30s --output /tmp/prof.json
rd-profiler analyze /tmp/prof.json --focus=scheduler,kernel
```

- Key metrics to inspect:
  - kernel_exec_ms (per-token)
  - scheduling_queue_ms
  - batch_fill_ms
  - kv_cache_hit_rate
  - gpu_utilization_pct
  - context_switches_per_sec (if using host threading)

4) Benchmarking suite — reproducible performance tests

- Location: infra/benchmarks/serving-suite in monorepo. The suite produces per-model profiles, per-device summaries, and per-release baselines.

- Standard benchmark commands:
```bash
# run microbench for a model on a target node
perf-bench run --model redwood-mistral-3b --device a100-80gb --seq-len 256 --batch 1 --duration 300 --output /artifacts/mistral-3b-a100-256-b1.json
# aggregate results
perf-bench aggregate --input /artifacts/*.json --baseline /benchmarks/baseline-2026-12-01.json --report /reports/bench-summary.html
```

- Benchmark outputs (table columns): model, device, seq_len, batch_size, tokens_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, peak_gpu_mem_mb.

- Baseline cadence: weekly nightlies and release gates for major runtime releases. Benchmarks are required for any kernel or scheduler change with potential perf impact > 2% token/sec deviation.

5) Release notes (runtime releases summary)

- 2026-06-01 - rdinferd v2.4: introduced fused_attn_v2 kernel, default balanced scheduler. +6-12% tokens/sec on small models.
- 2026-09-10 - rdinferd v2.6: int8 tensorcore path for supported GPUs (+18% throughput for quantized models).
- 2026-12-20 - rdinferd v3.0: KV-sharding, improved memory accounting, new telemetry for per-request kernel metrics.
- 2027-01-10 - rdinferd v3.1: scheduler bugfix for batch fill under preemptions; backported to Dedicated pools.

6) Known issues and mitigations

- Issue: rare p99 latency spikes during large canary rollouts (ticket INF-2982).
  - Symptoms: transient kernel selection fallback, increased batch_fill_ms.
  - Mitigation: set rd-router header X-RD-Rollout: safe and progressively ramp canary. If spike occurs, rollback to previous runtime version and throttle canary.

- Issue: int8 tensorcore path may produce degraded quality on some tails for Llama2-style architectures.
  - Mitigation: toggle kernel_selection: conservative for affected models and add model-specific quantization profile.

7) Runtime runbooks (incident steps)

- Runbook A: High p99 latency for model in Hosted pool
  1. Identify impacted model and nodes via dashboards (/dashboards/model-latency).
  2. Check rolling deploys in last 30 minutes (cdp events).
  3. Run rd-profiler collect --trace=short on one impacted node.
  4. If scheduling_queue_ms > 50ms: switch policy to latency-first for the pool:
     ```bash
     rdctl pool update --pool-id <pool> --scheduler.policy latency-first
     ```
  5. If kernel_exec_ms increased: capture kernel selection logs and open perf regression ticket; rollback runtime if needed.

- Runbook B: High GPU memory pressure / OOMs
  1. Check /var/log/nvidia/ for OOM traces.
  2. Evict low-priority tenants: rdctl evict --tenant <id> --priority low
  3. Lower batch_limit for affected nodes: rdctl node update --node <id> --batch_limit 8
  4. If persistent, drain node and schedule maintenance with infra.

8) Team wiki & ownership

- Primary owners: serving-runtime team (team alias: @eng-serving-runtime).
- Pager rotation: serving-runtime oncall (see /roster/serving-runtime).
- Related pages: architecture ADRs, kernel implementation docs, benchmarking dashboards.

9) Diagnostics & telemetry best practices

- Tag traces with model_id, deployment_id, kernel, and scheduler_policy. Example trace header: {"rd_model": "redwood-mistral-3b", "rd_kernel": "fused_attn_v2", "rd_sched": "balanced"}.
- Maintain daily perf baseline job that runs the core benchmark matrix at 03:00 UTC and alerts on >5% regression in tokens/sec for any model/device pair.

Appendix — quick references

- Logs: /var/log/rdinferd/runtime.log
- Profiler: rd-profiler (monorepo tool)
- Scheduler CLI: rdctl (ops tooling)
- Benchmarks: infra/benchmarks/serving-suite
- Owners: eng-serving-runtime@redwood.com

Diagram (text):
- Diagram: "Runtime request flow" — rd-router -> rdinferd (ingest) -> rd-sched (batching) -> kernel exec on GPU -> rd-kvcache lookups -> response. See architecture diagram on the wiki page /confluence/serving-runtime-architecture-diagram.

This document is a living playbook. For substantive changes to scheduler policies or kernel defaults, follow the release gating process: open PR -> attach benchmark runs (perf-bench outputs) -> reviewers: perf, serving-runtime, infra -> canary rollout -> graduation.
